header:
Date: 2025-11-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood attendees: Jordan Patel (AE), Maya Chen (SE), Ethan Ruiz (Product)
Customer attendees: Alex Rivera (Head of Product), Priya Singh (ML Platform Lead), Tom Bates (Security Architect)
Recording: Enabled
Notes: demo focused on Console + Optimize capabilities for evaluation, A/B/pairwise comparison, regression alerts, and integration with Zephyr's CI/CD
summary: Redwood team walked Zephyr through a live Console demo showing prompt set management, pairwise A/B comparisons using Optimize, and how regression alerts tie into prompt-based evaluations. Security and deployment questions (VPC/private vs hosted, SSO, audit logs) were discussed. Zephyr requested a trial workspace, baseline eval prompts, and security artifacts. Agreed to schedule POC kickoff with infra/security next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, joining with Maya and Ethan. Quick rolodex, can you each introduce yourselves?
[00:12] Alex: Alex here, Head of Product at Zephyr, thanks, excited to see the quality ops flow.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, ML Platform, we'll be running the POC.
[00:22] Tom: Tom, security. I'll be mostly asking the compliance-y questions.
[00:30] Jordan: Great. Today's agenda is a quick Console walkthrough — prompt sets, our Optimize pairwise and A/B comparison UI — and then how regression alerts work when you attach a prompt-set benchmark. We'll keep it practical, show a live prompt-set, and then discuss infra and security. Sound good?
[00:45] Alex: Yep, sounds good.
[00:50] Maya: I'll share my screen and open the Redwood Console. Tell me if the video is blurry for anyone.
[00:56] Priya: Looks good.
[01:05] Maya: Okay, starting on the Console home. This is the Experiments tab which houses prompt sets. Think of prompt sets as a canonical list of prompts and expected behaviors you want to track. You can group them by intent, product surface, or release.
[01:25] Alex: Quick Q: can prompt sets be versioned? We want traceability for audits.
[01:30] Maya: Yes — we have immutable snapshots whenever you 'lock' a prompt set for eval. They show in the history panel and you can reference a snapshot id. It's also included in the audit logs.
[01:40] Tom: Are those logs exportable to our SIEM?
[01:44] Maya: We have log-forwarding via webhook and S3 export; we also integrate with common log collectors. For private deployments you can keep logs inside your VPC.
[01:56] Jordan: Let's jump to building a pairwise comparison. I'm going to open a sample prompt-set for the 'customer support reply generation' flow.
[02:06] Maya: Here are five prompts — baseline, more concise, tone-shift, context-windowed, and safety-constrained. You can attach acceptance criteria per prompt, like F1 thresholds or pass/fail heuristics.
[02:22] Priya: Do you support custom metrics? We have a 'helpfulness' rubric that's a mix of BLEU-ish and human rating.
[02:28] Maya: Yep, you can define custom metrics and upload a small eval script. Our Optimize runner will compute those metrics across model outputs. There is a small sandbox for custom code that runs on Redwood-managed infra for hosted; for Dedicated/Private you can run the runner in your infra.
[02:45] Ethan: We're showing a pairwise comparison next — selecting two model variants and running 100 prompts to compare.
[02:52] [03:00] Maya: Starting the pairwise run now — the UI triggers parallel calls to the Redwood API, and you can see live pass rates. For latency-sensitive workloads, we also surface per-model median latency.
[03:15] Alex: How are you calling the models? Is it your hosted large models or a wrapper to other endpoints?
[03:21] Jordan: For hosted customers we run the model in Redwood's runtime; you can also register model endpoints from your infra or third-party providers and Redwood will route.
[03:30] Priya: Any throttling concerns when running large evals? We might want to run 10k prompts overnight.
[03:36] Maya: We recommend Dedicated for heavy eval throughput; the Console will let you schedule runs and choose a compute profile that attempts to keep costs down via batching and caching where applicable.
[03:48] Tom: Can regression alerts be thresholded on multiple metrics?
[03:51] Maya: Yes — you can create composite alert rules, e.g., if 'helpfulness' drops by >7% AND fail-rate increases by >5% over baseline. Alerts can post to Slack, PagerDuty, or trigger CI jobs.
[04:10] Alex: Show the A/B UX — where product managers might like to look at side-by-side diffs.
[04:16] Maya: Sure — switching to the A/B tab. This is the pairwise viewer where you see two outputs per prompt, inline diffs, and a quick 'winner' vote suggestion derived from your metric. You can annotate results and create a filtered view of 'disagreements' for human review.
[04:34] [04:50] Maya: I'm toggling the discrepancy filter to only show cases where metric delta is within +/- 0.1 so teams can prioritize noisy examples. You can also export the annotated subset as a CSV for manual QA.
[05:05] Priya: Nice — can the annotation workflow be integrated with our JIRA or Asana?
[05:11] Ethan: We have webhooks and a Zapier-like integration; for enterprise we can push directly to JIRA via API.
[05:20] Alex: About regression alerts — what's the cadence and data retention for the baseline? We need to retain baseline snapshots for vendor audits.
[05:28] Maya: Baselines are stored as immutable snapshots. Retention depends on plan; Dedicated and Private offer extended retention options and exports. For hosted, we default to 90 days but can extend for enterprise.
[05:42] Tom: What about model explainability — can we surface tokens or attention traces for reviewers?
[05:49] Maya: We surface token-level probabilities and n-best completions, not raw attention weights. For more detailed explainability you can plug in a local tool as part of the runner.
[06:02] [06:15] Jordan: Let's demo how alerts get triggered. I'm going to flip to Alerts config. Here you can create a rule: target prompt-set, metric, comparison window (rolling 7 days vs baseline snapshot). You can also scope by model or route.
[06:36] Maya: I'm creating an alert: helpfulness drop > 7% over snapshot 'v1.2' with severity 'major' and notify Slack channel #qa-alerts.
[06:48] Alex: And if an alert fires, can we automatically revert to a previous model?
[06:53] Maya: Yes — Redwood's rollout system supports automatic rollback. You can define an 'on-failure' policy to revert traffic to a pinned variant or route to a fallback model.
[07:06] Priya: Does rollback also lock the model version to prevent accidental promotion?
[07:10] Maya: You can pin a model and set policy to prevent promotion without manual approval.
[07:20] [07:30] Tom: Let's talk security for a minute; SSO, SAML, RBAC?
[07:35] Jordan: We support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. Cookie sessions can be short-lived and keys are rotated. We also have per-route RBAC and token scoping.
[07:50] Tom: KMS and encryption?
[07:53] Jordan: Data at rest is encrypted with keys managed by the cloud provider by default; for enterprise we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key.
[08:05] Tom: Audit trails?
[08:07] Maya: Detailed audit logs including snapshot ids, prompt changes, who triggered a rollout, and API calls are available. Exports can be pushed to your SIEM.
[08:20] Alex: On the technical deep-dive, how does the optimizer runner handle deterministic comparisons? We need consistent sampling seeds across runs.
[08:30] Ethan: Runner can lock RNG seeds and deterministic decoders; it also records the exact model binary, tokenization version, and runtime config in the snapshot metadata.
[08:45] Priya: Good. For the POC we'll want to run identical runs in our staging infra to confirm parity.
[08:51] Jordan: You can run Optimize both hosted and in Dedicated/Private modes so you can run the same runner close to data.
[09:00] [09:12] Maya: Back to the A/B viewer — here's a side-by-side where a prompt produced two outputs. You can open the 'explain' panel to see the token probs and our gated safety checks that flagged a response.
[09:30] Alex: There is a small typo in the example output (name swapped) — is there a deduping or entity fill guard?
[09:36] Maya: We have templating tokens and entity constraints you can enforce at runtime; plus our safety filters can block or rewrite.
[09:46] Priya: Are the prompt sets mutable by multiple users? We need branch workflows.
[09:51] Maya: There's branching and PR-like reviews for prompt sets. You can open a proposal, assign reviewers, and once approved lock the snapshot.
[10:05] [10:20] Jordan: Quick pause — any blockers so far?
[10:23] Tom: Security looks okay at a high level but want the SOC2/ISO docs. Also need clarity on where logs are stored in hosted.
[10:31] Jordan: We'll send the security whitepaper and the SOC2 report.
[10:35] Alex: For metrics, can we plug in our in-house 'helpfulness' scorer that requires callouts to a private model?
[10:42] Maya: Yes, you can register an external scorer; we have a runner plugin interface. For privacy you can host that scorer in your VPC and Redwood will call it over a secure channel.
[10:58] Priya: What about cost controls? We want to limit eval job spend.
[11:03] Ethan: There are per-run quotas, pre-flight cost estimates, and caps. Dedicated gives you more predictable pricing.
[11:16] [11:30] Maya: Now I'm showing the alert history. Here's a sample alert that fired last week in this demo account. You can see the metric delta, affected prompt count, and a roll-forward/rollback action.
[11:46] Alex: Can a PM subscribe only to alert summaries and not the raw outputs?
[11:50] Maya: Yep — notification templates can redact outputs and only show high-level metrics or attach a link to a protected review workspace.
[12:05] Tom: For private deployments, do you require outbound connections to Redwood control plane?
[12:11] Jordan: For the Private control plane you can opt for a fully offline control plane; otherwise lightweight telemetry can be configured over a customer-managed egress.
[12:24] Priya: Good to know.
[12:30] [12:40] Maya: I'm going to run a short live A/B of two prompt variants to show the guided review flow. Launching 50 prompts now.
[12:55] [13:20] Maya: Results populating — you can see the winner metric, and I'm flagging examples with 'helpfulness' disagreements.
[13:40] Alex: The UI suggests a winner even when the metric delta is small. Can you condition that on statistical significance?
[13:47] Maya: Yes — you can set a p-value threshold for automated winner assignment.
[14:05] Priya: How long does a 10k prompt run usually take?
[14:10] Maya: Depends on Dedicated capacity and batching profiles; with a medium cluster it could be 30-60 minutes; with heavy parallelism it's faster.
[14:22] Jordan: For overnight large evals, customers often schedule them off-peak and use cached prefixes to save cost.
[14:33] [14:45] Tom: If an alert triggers and we auto-roll back, do you keep a history of the rollback decision for audit?
[14:52] Maya: Yes — the action and who approved it are recorded in audit logs. The rollback itself can be configured as automated or manual.
[15:05] Alex: Show the API call for creating a prompt set and starting an Optimize job — we want to stash it into our CI.
[15:12] Ethan: Here's a sample curl that creates a prompt-set and a POST to start a job. We also supply SDKs in Python/Go/Node.
[15:28] Priya: Are tokens measured per hit or by output length? We need to estimate cost.
[15:34] Jordan: Usage is per input+output token for hosted; we provide pre-run estimates for Optimize jobs. Dedicated can be metered differently under contract.
[15:45] [15:55] Maya: I'm going to demo the report export. This exports a PDF with key metrics, annotated examples, and a CSV of disagreements.
[16:05] Alex: Great for stakeholder reviews.
[16:10] Tom: One more security question — do you do row-level encryption or field-level redaction? We have PII in prompts.
[16:17] Jordan: We support field-level redaction pipeline and recommended prompt-hygiene patterns; for PII you can scrub before sending or host in Private.
[16:28] Priya: We'll send some sample prompts with PII redaction rules for the POC.
[16:35] [16:50] Maya: Now hopping into the post-run analytics, you can filter by intent, by prompt text, by model, and see temporal trends. This lets you catch regressions that only affect a subset of intents.
[17:10] Alex: Can the regression engine run nightly and post a daily digest?
[17:14] Maya: Yes — scheduleable jobs and daily digest emails are supported. You can also push digests to Slack or Confluence.
[17:28] Jordan: Let's talk integration: you'll probably want Optimize jobs kicked off from your CI after model training or after a canary deploy?
[17:36] Priya: Exactly. Ideally after a canary we run a 1k prompt smoke test and if it passes, promote.
[17:43] Ethan: You can wire that up — our API has a 'compare against snapshot' endpoint to run quick checks.
[17:55] [18:10] Alex: For the POC, we're thinking: 3 weeks, run on Dedicated eval cluster, use 5k prompts, measure helpfulness/neutrality/safety. Can you support that?
[18:18] Jordan: Yes — we'll scope capacity and give a cost estimate.
[18:23] Tom: And share the SOC2 + penetration test summary.
[18:26] Jordan: Will do.
[18:30] [18:45] Maya: Small note on edge cases — if you have nondeterministic sampling, use seed-locking and deterministic decoders in the runner. Also be careful with temperature changes between runs.
[19:00] Priya: We'll lock those.
[19:06] Alex: Any limitations on the size of prompt sets? We have thousands of prompts across features.
[19:13] Maya: The Console can handle large prompt libraries; we recommend sharding into logical subsets to keep runs targeted.
[19:26] Jordan: I want to call out the fallback model routing again — good for graceful degradation during incidents.
[19:34] Priya: On that, how quickly can a rollback take effect?
[19:37] Maya: Rollbacks are near-instant for routing layer; full model warmup depends on cache but traffic redirection is immediate.
[19:46] [19:55] Alex: Can we do a hybrid where we store prompt sets in our git repo and Redwood pulls them?
[20:01] Ethan: We have a git-sync integration and can watch a repo for changes, create proposals, and require approvals before snapshotting.
[20:12] Priya: Excellent.
[20:20] [20:32] Tom: A quick compliance edge case — we need to ensure data residency in EU for a subset of prompts.
[20:38] Jordan: We can pin runs to a region and ensure data stays in-region for those snapshots. For Private, you can keep everything on-prem.
[20:52] Maya: I'm going to show the compare timeline — how metrics evolved across three snapshots. This is handy to visualize regressions introduced by model changes.
[21:08] Alex: Can we annotate a spike with release notes?
[21:11] Maya: Yes — annotations in the timeline are supported and show up in exports.
[21:20] [21:30] Jordan: We're about halfway through — any pressing questions?
[21:34] Alex: Curious about pricing - ballpark for a 3-week Dedicated eval cluster for 5k prompts?
[21:40] Ethan: We'll provide a written estimate but rough numbers depend on model size; we can propose a capped eval package for POCs.
[21:52] Priya: We'll accept a capped proposal.
[21:56] Tom: Also need a note about data purge after the POC.
[22:00] Jordan: We'll include data-retention and purge language in the proposal.
[22:06] [22:20] Maya: Showing the annotated disagreement reviewer — here's a queue you can assign to PMs or QA. They can accept a winner, escalate, or tag for a doc update.
[22:36] Alex: Does the reviewer UI support keyboard shortcuts? Our QA likes that.
[22:41] Maya: Yup, and you can bulk-accept if samples are consistent.
[22:50] Priya: For the POC we'll want weekly checkpoints with your CSM.
[22:54] Jordan: We'll pair you with a CSM.
[23:00] [23:12] Maya: Final quick demo: creating a composite alert across 3 metrics and configuring escalation to PagerDuty if major.
[23:30] Tom: Good. This is the sort of ops control we need.
[23:36] Alex: Anything we should be aware of re: model versions? We have custom fine-tuned models.
[23:43] Ethan: We can serve your fine-tuned models as artifacts in Dedicated; the runner records the exact artifact hash.
[23:55] Priya: Will we have to re-tokenize or refactor prompts for your runner?
[24:01] Maya: No — tokenization is recorded and we try to preserve parity; but part of the POC will confirm tokenization parity.
[24:10] [24:25] Jordan: Let's recap next steps: Jordan to provision trial workspace and send security docs; Maya to share deck and short clips; Zephyr to confirm stakeholder list and provide sample prompts. Anything else?
[24:37] Alex: Also schedule the infra/security kickoff.
[24:40] Jordan: Noted.
[24:45] Priya: One minor UX ask — a CSV import for prompt sets with metadata columns for intent, owner, and tags.
[24:54] Maya: We have that in beta, will enable for your workspace.
[25:05] [25:18] Alex: Alright, thanks team. Quick side question: any known gaps if we try to run this on-prem?
[25:24] Ethan: The main work is data egress and control plane connectivity if you opt-in; otherwise Private can be air-gapped with an on-prem runner. We'll help size infra.
[25:38] Tom: Pen test?
[25:40] Jordan: We can share recent penetration test summaries under NDA.
[25:47] [26:00] Maya: I'm going to pause the demo and hand back — any last live things you want to see?
[26:08] Priya: Can we see the API call for alert creation in Node?
[26:12] Ethan: Dropping a snippet in chat.
[26:20] Alex: Thanks. That helps our engineers.
[26:25] [26:40] Jordan: Okay, we'll follow up with the trial workspace and docs. Really appreciate the time.
[26:48] Alex: Thanks, Jordan and team. Excited to get started.
[26:55] Tom: Thanks. We'll review and send security questions.
[27:00] Priya: Bye everyone.
[27:05] [27:15] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional fill words removed for clarity; some product names slightly mis-transcribed earlier (e.g., 'Optimize' read as 'optimize runner' or 'optimizer' in a few places); timestamps are approximate.
